attempts.raw_response: Water the soil gently but thoroughly immediately after planting. Aim for moist, not soggy, conditions. For garden beds, maintain a spacing of about 4–6 inches (10–15 cm) between corms to allow for growth. In containers, ensure good drainage to prevent rot. Place the container or garden area in a location that receives full sun, as crocosmia thrive in bright light. Keep the soil consistently moist during the growing season, especially in dry spells. Mulching around the plants can help retain moisture and suppress weeds. With proper care, you should see sprouts emerge in a few weeks, followed by vibrant blooms in summer.

pair.human_continuation: Autumn is the growing season for your crocus corms. During this time, it is important to keep the soil moist, but not waterlogged.  Start by watering your corms 1-2 times per week. Several times a week, insert 2 fingers into the soil to gauge the moistness. If there is standing water more than a day after watering, begin watering just once a week. If your soil is completely dry (not moist) within a day, begin watering 3 times per week. If you live in an area with a short, warm spring, apply fertilizer to your corms in the early fall. If you live in an area with a long, temperate spring, apply fertilizer to your bulbs right after they flower.
pair.prefix: Use a trowel to dig small holes approximately 3–4 inches (7.6–10.2 cm) deep. Position each corm with the pointy end up, and place 1 corm in each hole. Cover each bulb with soil. If using containers, place your corm on top of the 5 inches (13 cm) of soil you already added to the container. Then cover your corms with another 2 inches (5.1 cm) of soil.
